written: 2026-11-12, before any result was computed or seen
question: On the companies of the current watchlists, did the third ranked highest by a measure return more over the following 12 months than the third ranked lowest?

measures.trend: close 21 bars ago divided by close 252 bars ago, minus 1 (adjusted closes, own currency); higher is better
measures.steady: minus the number of days in the last 756 bars with an absolute move of 5% or more while the region index (S&P 500 for tickers without a suffix, STOXX 600 otherwise) moved less than 2%; higher is better

universe: every ticker in config/watchlists.toml on the day of the run; a company enters a month once it has 756 bars of history
data: Yahoo adjusted daily closes, longest history available
formation: the last trading day of each calendar month
statistic: per formation month, mean outcome of the top third minus mean outcome of the bottom third; months with fewer than 12 companies having both values are left out; the reported number is the mean over months
interval: 90% moving-block bootstrap of the monthly series, blocks of 12 months, 5000 draws, seed 20261112
verdict: supported if the whole interval is above zero; otherwise not supported
runs: one run per measure; no parameter is changed after the result is seen; the result is shown on the page whatever it is
known_limits: survivorship: the universe is today's companies, so failures and delistings are missing and past returns look better than they were for an investor at the time
about 58 companies and overlapping 12-month outcomes: few independent observations, low power to detect a small effect
the companies were hand-picked into themed lists, not sampled
value and business quality cannot be tested: free data has no past fundamentals
